title: Check the Angle First

patient.name: Mdm Yeo Lai Kuan
patient.presenting_complaint: Charted for dilation, but has a history of narrow drainage angles

history.hpc: Mdm Yeo says 'Last time the doctor say my eye angle very narrow, must be careful.' She is charted for dilation today but mentions this narrow-angle history, which must be acted on before instilling any dilating drop.
history.pmhx: Known narrow anterior chamber angles. No drug allergies (confirm).

examination_findings.anterior_segment: Shallow anterior chambers / narrow angles by history — dilation could precipitate acute angle-closure

investigations.task: Recognise the narrow-angle contraindication and do not dilate until checked with the nurse/doctor
investigations.key_points: Confirm identity and the order; recognise the narrow-angle history as a contraindication; do not instil dilating drops; escalate to the nurse/doctor to confirm whether and how to dilate; document the history

diagnosis: The key step is recognising the narrow-angle history as a contraindication to routine dilation: dilating a narrow angle can precipitate acute angle-closure glaucoma. The OA withholds the dilating drops and checks with the nurse/doctor before proceeding, and documents the history. Patient safety is prioritised. This is a procedural/safety station.

immediate: Confirm identity and the dilation order
Recognise the narrow-angle history as a contraindication to routine dilation
Do NOT instil dilating drops at this point
Escalate to the nurse/doctor to confirm whether and how dilation should proceed
Only dilate if and as directed, then document pupil size, drops, dosage and time
Warn the patient to report any eye pain, headache or nausea urgently
follow_up: Doctor to decide on safe dilation or an alternative
Flag the narrow-angle history in the record
patient_education: Explain why dilation needs to be checked first given her angle history
Advise reporting eye pain, headache, nausea or haloes urgently
Reassure that her safety is the priority

key_points: Confirms identity and the dilation order
Withholds dilating drops because of the contraindication
Escalates to the nurse/doctor before proceeding
Only dilates if and as directed, with full documentation
Recognises narrow angles as a contraindication to dilation
Understands dilation could precipitate acute angle-closure glaucoma
Prioritises safety over completing the task
Knows to confirm with the doctor
Flags the narrow-angle history in the record
Warns the patient about acute glaucoma red flags
Documents the decision and any dilation given
